summary: Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley (~1964–1967) and studied under John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken. He served as a Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1989–2023).

Roy Rappaport worked in religious studies and anthropology, completing his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1998–2004) under Shlomo Biderman and earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2004–2011) under Gary A. Tubb. He joined the faculty of Tel Aviv University in ~2011.

Roy W. Perrett is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Canterbury (~1970–1975) and the University of Otago (~1978–1981). He held positions at Massey University (~1986–2005), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2003–2005), and the University of Melbourne (~2005–2010).

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at Harvard and Columbia, earning his doctorate under Donald Keene (~1967–1977). He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, and Oslo, before serving as head of the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila University, the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, and Sophia University. He held positions at Sophia, Ryukoku University, and Southern Methodist University (1989).
Rudolf Geiger studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1913–1919) and held a post at the University of Munich (~1948–1963).

Rudolf Haym worked in philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1839), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1841–1843), later holding a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky worked in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, he taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt and held an academic post at the University of Bonn (1974–2004).
Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1923).
Rudolf Much was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1882–1887) and later held an academic post there (~1895–1934).

Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1888–1891) and under Richard von Garbe, later holding posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).
Rudolf Seydel was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1855–1858) and subsequently held an academic post there (~1860–1892).

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1877–1879) and under Heinrich Zimmer (~1881–1882). He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), the University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and the University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald (~1839–1843) and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843–1844). He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent from 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist and historian who earned degrees from Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala, Curator at Mysore's Oriental Research Institute, and Director of the Karnataka State Archaeology Department.

Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen completed an MA under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, earned a PhD at Leiden University under Paul Harrison (attested 2018), and is affiliated with Peking University (attested 2026).

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and held a long-term academic post at Yale University (~1945–1989).

Rupert Gethin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. He held posts at the University of Bristol (from 1987), the Pali Text Society, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.
